name: Rapid Ads
tagline: AI tooling for spinning up paid ad creative and copy variants fast, without a designer in the loop.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The generative core here is not the hard part: feed a product URL to an LLM, get twenty headline and body variants, composite them onto a few layout templates, export at every required pixel size. An agent can do that in a weekend and the output will be roughly as mediocre as most tools in this space, which is to say usable. What you will not get in one sitting is the plumbing: Meta and Google ad account OAuth, asset library management, video rendering, and any feedback loop that ties creative to actual spend performance. If your workflow is 'generate a batch, eyeball it, upload manually', the DIY version is genuinely fine. If your workflow is 'push live to three ad accounts and track which variant won', pay someone.
coreLoopDIY: Scrapes a product page, generates ad copy variants with an LLM, and composites them onto layout templates exported at standard ad sizes.
requirements: Your own fonts, logo, and product images
Optional headless browser for scraping product pages
whatYouLose: Direct publishing into Meta, Google, or TikTok ad accounts, OAuth and review policy included
Any performance feedback loop, so no data on which variant actually converts
Video and animated creative, which is a separate and much larger build
Template craft: hand-built layouts look hand-built, and ad platforms punish ugly
Someone else keeping up with changing aspect ratios and placement specs
moatNotes: The defensible part of any ad tool is the boring API surface with the ad platforms plus whatever it learns from creative that actually performed.
whyPeopleStillPay: Ad creative is volume work with a deadline attached, and the value of a tool like this is that it removes friction on a Tuesday afternoon when you need fifteen variants live by Thursday. A local script does the generation, but it does not do the uploading, the placement specs, the naming conventions, or the version you need in 9:16 because someone decided Reels matters this quarter. People pay to not think about any of that, and to have a single place where last month's creative still lives.
notes: Generating ad copy is a solved commodity; getting it into an ad account without hating your life is the actual product.
prompt:
Build a local ad creative generator. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, sharp for image compositing, better-sqlite3 for local storage. Everything runs on localhost with `npm run dev`.

Features, in scope:
1. A form that takes a product URL plus optional manual overrides for product name, audience, and tone.
2. A server action that fetches the URL, strips it to readable text with a simple HTML-to-text pass, and sends it to an LLM (read OPENAI_API_KEY from .env, model choice in one config constant).
3. The LLM returns structured JSON: 10 headlines (max 40 chars), 10 primary texts (max 125 chars), 5 CTA button labels. Validate with zod, retry once on parse failure.
4. A templates folder with three hand-coded layout functions: image-top with text block, full-bleed image with text overlay and scrim, and solid color card with logo. Each takes text plus an image path plus a size.
5. Render with sharp and an SVG text layer at four sizes: 1080x1080, 1080x1350, 1200x628, 1080x1920. Handle text wrapping and shrink font size to fit rather than overflowing.
6. Local asset library: drag and drop product images and a logo into /public/assets, list them in SQLite, pick them per render.
7. Results grid showing every variant with a download button plus a "download all as zip" action.
8. Save each generation batch to SQLite so you can reopen it later.

Out of scope, do not build: ad platform OAuth, publishing to Meta or Google, video or animation, multi user auth, performance tracking, a hosted deployment.

Include a .env.example, a README with setup steps, and two starter fonts in /public/fonts with the paths wired up. Use real placeholder assets so `npm run dev` produces output on first run without configuration beyond the API key.
